note: First Indian Governor-General (C. Rajagopalachari): primary chapter HIS-27, alt HIS-28. Neither fetched source (NCERT leps201 Ch.1; IGNOU BHIC-113 Units 20-21) states who became the first Indian Governor-General, so it is not taught here. WBBSE e-textbook unreachable from this machine.

Number of princely states at Partition: the chapter teaches NCERT leps201's figure of 565 (s4, claim c22), but this PYQ's options (555/558/560/562) do not include 565, so the item as keyed is not taught. The discrepancy is disclosed openly in s4's deep text and exam_note box.
Hind Mazdoor Sangh founder: mapped alt is OUT_OF_SCOPE (trade-union movement). Not in this chapter's scope and not covered by the fetched sources.

First Governor-General of Pakistan (Muhammad Ali Jinnah): IGNOU BHIC-113 (c48) records only that Jinnah refused to let Mountbatten be a common Governor-General of India and Pakistan; it does not state that Jinnah himself became Pakistan's first Governor-General. Not asserted from the fetched sources.

'Tryst with destiny' speech: taught in s1 — Nehru, the first Prime Minister of free India, addressed the Constituent Assembly at midnight on 14-15 August 1947 (NCERT leps201 p. 3; claim c01). Primary chapter HIS-26, also in this chapter's scope.

Boundary demarcated by Sir Cyril Radcliffe: the fetched sources name only the Boundary Commission (its delayed award is taught in s2, claim c49); Radcliffe's name appears in neither NCERT leps201 Ch.1 nor IGNOU BHIC-113 Units 20-21. Disclosed in s2's exam_note box; not taught.
First Indian Governor-General of free India (C. Rajagopalachari): same gap as IDO-2019-Q54 — not stated in the fetched allowed sources; WBBSE unreachable.

Operation Polo (Hyderabad): the underlying event IS taught in s5 — Indian army moved in during September 1948 and the Nizam surrendered (claim c32) — but the code name 'Operation Polo' appears in neither fetched source, so the item as asked is marked untaught. Disclosed in s5's exam_note box.
Last Governor-General of independent India (C. Rajagopalachari): Governor-General succession is not covered by the fetched NCERT/IGNOU sources; not taught.
First Indian Governor-General (C. Rajagopalachari): same Governor-General gap as above; not taught.
Gandhi assassination date (30 January 1948): taught in s3 — Godse shot Gandhiji during evening prayer in Delhi on 30 January 1948 (NCERT leps201 p. 12; claim c19). Primary chapter HIS-28.

Sikkim became a full-fledged state in 1975: NCERT leps201's reorganisation narrative (fetched in full) does not include Sikkim, and no fetched IGNOU/NIOS/e-PG source covering Sikkim's 1975 statehood was obtained. Not taught; recorded as a source gap.
